external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal using vendor-issued credentials.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The SaaS vendor hosts the supplier document portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes the records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account receiving the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Supplier signs in to the supplier document portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload compliance paperwork
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads compliance paperwork and staff contact details to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: Category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and supplier staff contact details

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores uploaded supplier documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance documents and staff contact details

data_flows.name: push data extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The description says the extract is encrypted end to end, while the landing-bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_flows.name: load data extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and vendor platform.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform contains confidential data because it stores supplier compliance documents and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the vendor platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket contains confidential data because it receives the supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the bucket receives a supplier data extract containing supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database contains confidential data because it stores supplier records derived from the extract.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
